column1: # Classification of every row in docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, 2026-08-02. Working artifact for the
# left-arm rebuild (#33). READ-ONLY analysis — no ledger row was edited to produce this.
# REQ      a testable behaviour of the product. One observable thing; belongs in requirements.yaml.
# PRIN     a product principle or posture. True across the whole system, no single test can hold it.
#          These are the closest thing this repo has to NEEDS — they are why the product is shaped
#          as it is — but most are written as constraints rather than as what the owner wanted.
# ADR      a decision, an architecture choice, or a rejected option. History, not a requirement.
#          "Decided against X" rows are the clearest cases: nothing to verify, only to remember.
# RETIRED  already marked ⚰️. Belongs in adr/ as superseded history.

column3: wide-audience product; generic rules are load-bearing
the ledger is the source of truth (meta-process, not product behaviour)
token efficiency is a value; explicitly NOT enforced as an NFR any more
recommendation posture — overlaps R49 and R80
the plugin is self-contained under its own root
hooks are best-effort and never break the triggering action
tq owns its store; never native task tools
non-technical-owner posture — autonomy vs consent line
decided against a plugin-owned destructive-action gate
decided against consolidating the plugins — later reversed
architecture: one steering document + a tiny enforced core
autopilot is enforced and persisted per repo
the hook/steering boundary is decided by a component's nature
under autopilot, taste choices are parked not auto-decided
ship-mode auto-commits to a work branch
ship-it merges to default and prunes merged branches
resume is a triage handoff, class-preserving
parked/blocked is a prefix-view, never a status value
the secret gate covers every content-writing tool
tab-delimited reads — superseded by the US separator
tq report is compact and never renders done_when
the suite is the executable half of the enforced core
the recommendation contract — overlaps R5 and R80
per-repo flags gate the enforced core; fail-safe lock
the product is the propose to queue to drain loop
redesign logs UX and quality attributes only
complete the behaviour net before whole-app redesign
anti-drift gate on flow test references
task-store scoping keys on a per-worktree identity
no plugin-generated file at a governed repo's root
the open queue stays minimal-blast; decompose-park
domain context arrives via MCP; truth flows inward
injected artifacts are byte-capped; steering is two-tier
the cap moved 12288 to 6144 to 6656 (history + withdrawn claims)
the deterministic spine runs on a rail
a command's parameters are visible where it is invoked
the status line shows account rate-limit usage
the mutation gate refuses to certify what it did not observe
a watch that gives up does not report success
the posture is a stated default; the verdict is unconditional
a hook's cost stays bounded, and the bound is measured
a review is transparent to autopilot
